text: Q1 The signal conditioning circuit shown in Figure Q1 is the basis for an acoustic direction finder. Input nodes M1 and M2 are connected to microphones that detect the difference in sound pressure arriving at each. If the acoustic signal arriving at each microphone is of the same amplitude and in phase, the signals at nodes 'A' and 'B' are equal and no output appears at the output of the difference circuit, hence it can be determined that the source is equidistant from each microphone. Similarly, if the signals are phase shifted, the amplitude and phase of the signals are used to calculate the direction of the source. The circuit consists of two non-inverting buffer amplifiers (A1, A2) with adjustable gain followed by a difference amplifier circuit around A3. The output of the signal conditioning circuit 'Vout' is connected to an embedded processor to perform the calculations. You may assume that all the operational amplifiers are of good quality with negligible offset voltage, offset current, bias current, and have high gain. They are also capable of output signal swings up to the power rails (+/- 5V). Figure Q1 Due to production variations, individual microphone sensitivity (measured in mV / Pa) can vary by +/- 20%. This is shown in Figure Q1 by the microphone attached to input 'M1' having a sensitivity of 2.0mV/Pa while the microphone attached to input 'M2' has a sensitivity of 2.5mV/Pa. (a) For a sinusoidal sound pressure wave of +/- 1.5 Pa (peak) appearing at the microphones, calculate the values of R2 and R4 such that the signals appearing at nodes 'A' and 'B' are identical and = 1.0Vrms. Show all workings and state any assumptions. Page 2 of 9
